id: Two Psychics and a Medium-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Two Psychics and a Medium
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Following sold-out performances across Australia and New Zealand, ‘Two Psychics and a Medium’ is back. Catch the show at The Opera House as part of the ‘Eternal World Tour’. Psychic mediums Julia Cartagena and Anthony Grzelka star in the live theatre experience. There are no scripts and no pre-selected participants, so every show is unique. Julia and Anthony connect with audience members in real time. You can expect readings, laughs, and powerful moments of connection. 

Alongside being a psychic medium, Julia is an author and inspirational speaker. For over two decades, she’s held readings for a range of clients: from celebrities to business leaders. Anthony is a psychic medium, author, and spiritual communicator known as Australia’s ‘Ghost Whisperer’. He reports he experienced spiritual guidance from spirits as early as five years old. Since then, he’s turned it into his career. He was the first medium in Australia to give live audience readings, and he’s often appearing on television. Together, Julia and Anthony’s personal messages leave audiences feeling comforted and inspired.

id: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
The traditional sound of Appalachian music. bluegrass, country, Americana, and folk will fill the Michael Fowler Centre in February. American singer-songwriters Gillian Welch and David Rawlings blend the traditional music practices together in their first New Zealand concert in over a decade. The partners on stage and in life have 30 years of experience collaborating over haunting covers of folk greats. You might hear songs like Look at Miss Ohio, Orphan Girl, and Empty Trainload of Sky. Expect sparse magical arrangements and exquisite lyricism. 

Since their last visit to Wellington, they've been busy writing and producing music. Their recent album, ‘Woodland’, is the first attributed to both of them. Despite collaborating on most things, previous albums were billed individually. The album shares the name of their Nashville studio Woodland, lost to a tornado in 2020. 

You might recognise Gillian’s voice from the Coen brothers film ‘O Brother, Where Art Thou?’. She contributed to the soundtrack and snuck into the film itself. David is also a record producer and fronts the band Dave Rawlings Machine. Together, the pair are winners of multiple Grammy Awards and a slew of other accolades.

id: Kneecap-TSB Arena, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Kneecap
long_description:
A blend of Irish-language rap and sharp social commentary has built an international following for Kneecap . The hip-hop trio, made up of Mo Chara, Móglaí Bap, and DJ Próvaí, made a name for itself with raucous live performances. Formed in Belfast in 2017, Kneecap’s popularity skyrocketed following the release of the 2024 biographical film ‘Kneecap’ in which the group’s members each played themselves. Their previous visit to Wellington in 2025 was described by The Post as “explosive”, with the crowd eating out of the palm of their hand from the moment they took the stage. 

That tour was followed in 2026 by the release of third album ‘Fenian’ which has seen the group expand its sound to something darker and even more controversial. The trio will be joined in Wellington’s TSB Arena in February by Aotearoa’s own DJ, producer, and artist Lady Shaka. Expect a night of high-energy hip-hop, razor-sharp lyrics, and one of the most talked-about live shows on the touring circuit.

id: Randy Feltface — Gimmick-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Randy Feltface — Gimmick
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
He’s purple, has no eyebrows, and is made of felt. Randy Feltface is an Australian puppet comedian. After two decades collecting awards and critical praise around the world, he opens his ‘Gimmick’ tour in Wellington. Come down to The Opera House for a silly and self-hour hour of laughs. 

Randy Feltface has spent his career denying the accusation that he is a gimmick. Now, he says it’s time to own it. Expect a show that blends existential dread, cultural commentary and relentless punchlines. 

The creator of Randy Feltface, Heath McIvor, has amassed a devoted following across the globe. He’s a regular fixture on Australian television and the international stand-up comedy circuit. Heath has written and performed a dozen solo stand-up comedy shows, released seven comedy specials and has a Netflix special.

name: Bee in the City
long_description:
In Spring, Wellington transforms into a vibrant outdoor art gallery to raise funds for LifeFlight. The bee trail is perfect for a fun, free, family-friendly day out. Download the app or pick up a map from The Enormous Crocodile Company bike shop on Herd Street. Bee in the know about where to go, tick off sculptures, earn rewards, and discover new corners of the waterfront. 

New Zealand artists and community groups have designed each sculpture to uniquely tell the story of Aotearoa. Keep an eye out for local artist Ariki Brightwell’s ‘Ngaro huruhuru’, inspired by our native bee. Found a favourite? When the trail ends, you can bid for the artwork and take it home. Auction proceeds will contribute to LifeFlight’s lifesaving work, including the Westpac Rescue Helicopter.
